why: A first-party component set that connects form validation, recoverable error messaging, and skeleton loading to explicit follow-up actions and assistive-technology behavior. It is useful for treating transient and blocking states as part of the same task contract rather than as isolated visual variants.

states.title: Field validation with a visible correction route
states.evidence: Fluent Field changes the field presentation for validation and provides a validation message that describes the state and guides the person forward.

states.title: Error message bars include recovery actions
states.evidence: Fluent specifies that an error message bar represents a failure that must be addressed before continuing and includes a button or link to resolve it.

states.title: Skeletons preserve structure while content is pending
states.evidence: Fluent uses skeletons for dynamic content and recommends reflecting only the stable high-level information people can expect after loading.

transitions.contract: Keep the label and field perceivable, make the invalid state visible, and describe the correction needed beside the control.
Place the message near the affected scope and expose a concrete button or link instead of leaving a dead end.
Represent the stable shape while loading, then preserve keyboard context when the real content becomes available.

recovery.pattern: Use a brief validation message that names the condition and tells the person how to proceed.
Use an error message bar with a resolution action; do not make the recovery path implicit.

recovery.scenario: Several loading regions finish at different times
recovery.pattern: Coordinate announcements with aria-busy so screen-reader users do not receive partial or noisy completion updates.

accessibility.evidence: Fluent keeps labels enabled for assistive technology and exposes required fields to screen readers; validation messages provide forward guidance.
Fluent uses assertive live announcements for error and warning message bars, while informational and success messages are polite.
Fluent advises an accessible name for focusable loading content and suggests live regions or aria-busy for important skeleton updates without disrupting focus.

capture.reusePolicy: inspiration-only — record the documented state, recovery, and accessibility contracts without copying Fluent components, code, icons, illustrations, or brand assets.
